 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO i) ISSUE A WRIT OF CERTIORARI QUASHING THE GENERAL AWARD BEARING NO.KIADB.LAQ.NO.1279/2022-23 DATED 05.01.2023 PASSED BY 3RD RESPONDENT IN RESPECT OF LAND BEARING SY.NO.13/1 MEASURING 0.23 GUNTAS,
SITUATED AT OBALAPURA VILLAGE, THYAMAGONDLU HOBLI,
NELAMANGALA TAUK, BANGALORE RURAL DISTRICT OF PETITIONER IS CONCERNED, WHICH IS PRODUCED AT ANNEXURE-C AND ETC.
 THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The present petition is filed by the petitioner seeking for a writ of certiorari to quash the general award passed by respondent No.3-KIADB on 05.01.2023 in respect of NC: 2023:KHC:33310 property bearing Survey No.13/1, measuring 0.23 guntas situated at Obalapura Village,
Thyamagoundlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore Rural District and for a further direction to the respondents to consider the case of the petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, 1966.

2 2.

entities.text: Sri. Byregowda vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that though as on the date the general award was passed there was neither any litigation pending nor was there any impediment for the respondents to pass the consent award as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, 1966, the Respondent No.3 proceeded to pass the general award and that in view of the law laid down in Smt. Rathnamma vs. The State of Karnataka in W.P.No.31702/2018 dated 29.11.2018 passing of the consent award under Section 29(2) is not only beneficial but would also put an end to the challenge to the award.

entities.text: Smt. Rathnamma vs. The State of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he submits that the general award in the circumstances be set aside and the respondents be directed to pass the consent award.

In response, Sri.P.V.Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondents -KIADB submits that the petitioner did not come forward to claim the compensation and he further submits that the issue involved in the present petition is covered by the order dated 29.11.2018 passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.31702/2018.
He further submits the present petition may also be disposed of, subject to the directions issued in the said order.

4. Heard and perused the records.
5.

Under the identical circumstances, this Court in its order dated 29.11.2018 passed in W.P.31702/2018 while allowing the writ petition, has issued following directions:
"4.

In view of the above, this writ petition succeeds in terms of the decision cited above; a Writ of Certiorari issues quashing the impugned award dated 13.4.2017 at Annexure-E so far as it relates to the lands of the petitioner only for the purpose of determination and payment of the compensation as if the award is by agreement under Section 29 (2) NC: 2023:KHC:33310 of the Act, leaving the vested title to the land in the respondent-KIADB, otherwise unaffected".
6.
In that view of the matter, petitioner is also entitled to the benefit of similar order.

Hence, the following:
ORDER 1. The writ petition is allowed.
2. The general award dated 05.01.2023 as per Annexure-C insofar as it relates to the extent of the petitioner's land is hereby set aside.

3. The respondents are directed to consider the case of the petitioner in terms of the order/directions extracted herein above within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

Sd/-
